Only when the synonym is reaching some threshold that it is split into another subvoat, based on decision of mods / user. The effect? It will reduce the mods needed for small subvoat. More smaller subvoat can be accomodated.

I'm a latecomer to the series. After reading the books, I have to ask that question: why did Rowling write this character? He's totally useless. Rowling should have focused on Harry and Hermione.

Any thoughts?

Hey, that's a really good question! Here's my two cents:

Ron was totally necessary for Harry to have an "in" to Wizarding culture beyond school. I just reread PS last night, and honestly, Hermione wasn't really even human until they're taking on Neville. Ron is the one who bonds with Harry, who teaches Harry about the smaller, more human things that comes with being a wizard (Quidditch and chess are the two big ones--and while he likely could've learned those without Ron, it doesn't make sense from a storytelling perspective for Harry to up and hear about Quidditch for the second time from McGonagall and Wood).

While the series progresses, oftentimes Ron is Harry's shoulder to lean on, especially when the boys are mad at Hermione, or when Hermione is of no assistance, like with the Firebolt or the Yule Ball. Ron doesn't have Hermione's intelligence, Ron doesn't have the typical Gryffindor bravado, but Ron humanizes the trio.

I think Ron is a huge factor in Harry wanting to go Gryffindor rather than Slytherin. The only two kids to really approach him were Ron and Draco. itsBS and MisterLovegood have it right, Ron was Harry's connection to the wizarding world. If not him then it would have been Draco, who would have been an ass when it came to asking basic questions and getting answers.

Note: it's been a while since I've read the books, but Ron and by extension his family help a lot with the plot and with Harry's development. They're essentially the family he wished he's had and Ron serves as a good foil for Harry. Also, Ron and his father serve as exposition, explaining how the world works.

I think in addition to all that was said he also brings some humor into the story as well, whether it be him or his family. Kind of what would be regular ole everyday family humor, though they are wizards. They bring the human element.

I don't think that Ron was entirely superfluous, but at the same time, I do think that some of the drama and angst involving him was redundant. One of my least favorite things about Deathly Hallows was the way that the Harry/Ron rivalry and fighting boiled back up. I didn't enjoy it in Goblet, and I didn't need it to float to the surface again in the 11th hour. It took us nowhere, and belabored an already involved story.
